title: Restaurant managers lose hours to unplanned admin, and manual inventory counting and receiving drive food-cost variance

history.reason: Initial evidence collected in the first discovery session (issue #7)

description: Restaurant general managers absorb a heavy reactive administrative load — call-outs, payroll fixes, last-minute schedule changes — with 44% of operators reporting six or more unplanned admin hours per GM per week. In parallel, inventory control remains substantially manual: receiving and counting errors are the second-ranked driver of inventory variance (37% of operators), behind only waste/spoilage. Operators with disciplined forecasting and consistent tool use report far less unplanned admin, which suggests the pain concentrates in lower-maturity operations rather than being uniform.
customer_segment: US restaurant operators. The benchmark sample skews to multi-unit brands (over half oversee 20+ locations); single-unit independent restaurants — a core small-business segment — are underrepresented and their load is unmeasured here.
context: Food and labor are the dominant restaurant cost lines, so inventory variance shows up directly as margin loss on thin (often single-digit) margins. The same report links unplanned admin load to GM/AGM turnover, making the administrative burden a retention problem as well as a time problem.

evidence.text: 44% of operators report GMs spending six or more hours per week on unplanned administrative tasks.
Receiving/counting errors (37%) and inaccurate forecasting/ordering (26%) are among the top drivers of inventory variance, behind waste or spoilage (54%).
Operators with under 5% sales forecast variance are far more likely to report under five unplanned admin hours weekly (74%) than operators with 16%+ variance (22%).
Higher unplanned admin tracks higher GM/AGM turnover (5% high turnover at low admin loads versus 15% at 6-10 unplanned hours).

alternatives: Paper and spreadsheet inventory counts (status quo for many operators)
Standardized forecasting systems and fixed admin routines (the top-tier operators' pattern in the same report)
Spot-check counting of high-variance items instead of full counts

contradictory_evidence.text: The burden is uneven: top-quartile operators with consistent tool discipline report low unplanned admin — this may be primarily a process-discipline problem in lower-maturity operations, not a universal missing-tool problem.
The evidence comes from a small (n=112), multi-unit-skewed, vendor-framework survey; it may overstate how structured the typical independent restaurant's problem is, or miss it entirely.

uncertainty: No independent or independent-restaurant-specific time-use data yet. Inventory-specific hours are bundled into general unplanned admin in this source, so the size of the inventory-counting slice alone is unknown.
open_questions: How much time do single-unit independent restaurants actually spend counting, receiving, and reconciling inventory each week, and in what tools (paper, Excel, POS)?
Is the felt pain margin loss from variance, manager time, or both?
What do independents already pay for back-office software, if anything?
next_actions: Seek National Restaurant Association operator data and any academic or government time-use evidence focused on independent restaurants before deepening.
Treat any vendor 'hours on inventory' claims as reported, not observed, until independently corroborated.
